title: Any timeline row that holds sub-layers expands and collapses like the Layers list
goal: On the timeline, anything made of parts (a title page with its title and subtitle, a name card, a group, a component, a logo with layers, a Size measurement group) has a disclosure arrow like the Layers list. Expanded, each sub-layer is its own indented row with its own bar, so it can be picked, retimed, keyed and changed independently; collapsed, it is one row. The behaviour and look match the Layers list so the two read as one system.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-17): "I think it would be nice to have timeline rows with sub layers like title/subtitle should be expandable/collapsible similar to layers, and you can tweak those elements independently." Follows the user's report the same morning that the subtitle could not be retimed because it is not a sub element of the title page (a-title-page-s-parts-each-have-their-own-labelle, seq 1, already in progress).

From code reading: track rows already have a disclosure twist (Sources/Photonz/TimelineTrackRows.swift:225, :293-304) and folded/open heights (:1286-1297, :1425) for a layer's motion lanes and group tracks; the Layers list's disclosure lives in LayersListView.swift. Reuse those; do not invent a second disclosure look.
acceptance: Builds on a-title-page-s-parts-each-have-their-own-labelle (title parts as labelled rows, in progress when this was filed): generalise that to every layer with children, one shared implementation, not a title-only path

A disclosure arrow on any timeline row whose layer has children; click (or Option-click to expand all levels, as in the Layers list), Right/Left arrow keys on a picked row expand and collapse; nested children indent one step per level, like the Layers list

Each child row shows the child's name and kind icon and its own bar for when it is on screen; picking it picks that child on the canvas and shows its own panel sections; dragging its bar's ends or middle changes only that child's timing; its keys and animated property lanes appear under it when it is expanded further
Expanded or collapsed state is remembered per layer in the document, and mirrors the Layers list (expanding in one expands in the other) unless the audit argues they should be separate
Collapsed, a parent row shows a faint summary of where its children's timings fall (thin marks) so retiming is discoverable
No zoom of the timeline or canvas changes when expanding, collapsing or dragging child bars (MEASURED)
Works for title pages, name cards, groups, components, logos with layers and Size measurement groups at Next defaults
A walk expands a title page, retimes the Subtitle, collapses it, expands a group two levels deep and moves a grandchild's bar
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: USER 2026-10-17 follow-ups: "i want to support sub layers" and "not every row would have sub layers". So: sub-layers are a general timeline concept (any layer that has children shows them nested), not a title special case; a row whose layer has no children shows NO disclosure arrow and keeps today's look and height (no empty indent, no placeholder). The walk must check a plain clip row has no arrow.

USER 2026-10-17, the model to build to: "but components with parts would? the timeline is similar to the layers pane, but it allows you to adjust horizontally on a timeline when it appears and how it transitions". So the timeline IS the Layers list with a time axis: the same rows, the same nesting and order, the same names and icons; components with parts show their parts as sub-rows; every row adds a horizontal bar for when that layer is on screen and its in and out transitions (drawn as the bar's shaded ends, draggable). Write this sentence into the design rules (UX-PATTERNS placement contract, Timeline row) and keep the two views in step (expanding, renaming, reordering in one shows in the other).

Adversarial pass before building: (1) The timeline already shows a picked part's row and a title track's arrow opens all parts; a generic tree must not bury the tracks below, so rows open only by an arrow, and a pick still shows just the picked part's chain when closed (the rule the title task kept after walks broke). (2) Plain Right/Left are Premiere's frame step on a video and Photoshop's nudge with a layer picked, so per UX-PATTERNS §7 expand/collapse does not take them: the arrow and Option-click (all levels) open rows. (3) A part of a group placed in time has no stretch of its own (placeInTime refuses one, because a part with absolute times is left behind when its parent moves). So a part's own time is new model: a stretch on the clock of the thing it is inside, so it travels with the parent, plus a shift so sliding a part carries its keys (After Effects' layer bar). (4) The Layers list is hidden while the timeline is open on a video (TimelineIsTheLayerList), so one open set shared by both is the honest mirror; it is remembered per file the way the list's is, not in the document, since opening a row must not be an undo step or mark the file edited. (5) A copy of a component has its contents rewritten from its original, so its parts are listed but their bars do not drag (an edit would be lost on the next sync). (6) Premiere/AE: a nested comp twirls open with its layers indented and their own bars; this matches it.

Built: PhotonzCore LayerPartTime (a part's own stretch on the clock of the thing it is inside, shift so a slide carries its keys; drawn/strip honour it; 15 tests) and TimelineChildRows (the row tree from the Layers list's order and open set, picked chain under a closed row, every-level open, closed-row marks; 8 tests). App: the track arrow opens any clip with parts (was title-only), child rows indent one Layers-list step per level with their own arrow (Option = every level), name and kind icon, and a bar: title part bar, own-time clip bar, or the new TimelinePartBar (ends and middle retime, snaps, one undo). Open state is expandedGroupIDs shared with the Layers list; a pick no longer opens groups while the timeline stands in for the list. Walk steps dragPart, markZoom, expectZoomSteady; dragClip finds own-time parts on open rows.

Verified: Scripts/test.sh 13555 tests green. timeline-sub-layer-rows-walk green at Next defaults (no flags): V1 has no arrow; title opens with zoom unchanged (markZoom/expectZoomSteady); Subtitle start +0.5s -> 1.5s; closed again; three rectangles grouped two deep, track and inner group opened by their arrows clicked at their faces, grandchild Rectangle slid +1s to 2.0s with Rectangle 2 unmoved and no zoom change; Option-click closes and opens every level. 14 related walks and 24 timeline walks green. Pictures looked at: 1-title-closed (marks on foot of title bar), 2/3 (part rows, Subtitle at 1.5s), 6 (two levels, indented), 7 (grandchild moved, groups' bars follow), 8 (every level open). Fixed timeline-right-click-menus-walk, which failed after another walk left keys on the clipboard (it passes alone): clearClipboard at its start.

Left rough (not filed): a part's moving-value lane labels sit at the left margin, not indented (cosmetic, in the audit's evaluate); Escape does not call off a part bar drag (undo covers it, same as title parts); a part with its own stretch taken out of its group by Ungroup keeps a stretch nothing reads (it shows the whole time, nothing lost); component copies' parts list but do not drag (by design, sync would undo it). Not verified at defaults: logos (an SVG/PNG lands as one picture, no layers to open) and Size measurement groups on a video (not tried). Arrow keys: per UX-PATTERNS §7 Right/Left stay frame step/nudge.
